items.title: Pristine Light
items.description: Paper, cream, off-white grounds with dark ink text. Airy, editorial, high-contrast on white rather than a dark-mode default.

items.title: Deep Dark
items.description: Charcoal and graphite grounds. Overused as a default - only pick this when it carries a real twist (unusual accent, texture, or light treatment), not as the safe choice.

items.title: Bold Studio Solid
items.description: A decisive solid color field - oxblood, royal blue, forest, vermilion, emerald - carrying the whole page rather than a neutral ground plus accent.

items.title: Quiet Premium Neutral
items.description: Bone, sand, taupe, stone, smoke. Restrained and material-led rather than stark light or dark.

items.title: Technical grid / dot field
items.description: A faint structural grid or dot field reads as precision-engineered rather than decorative.

items.title: Solid with soft ambient depth
items.description: A near-solid ground with subtle gradient or light falloff for depth, no hard graphic elements.

items.title: Full-bleed cinematic imagery
items.description: Photographic or rendered imagery fills the section edge to edge; copy sits in the image's negative space.

items.title: Tactile paper / material texture
items.description: A physical-material texture (paper grain, fabric, stone) grounds the section instead of a flat digital fill.

items.title: Clean grotesk
items.description: Satoshi-like: a neutral, contemporary sans with even proportions - reads modern without a strong personality of its own.

items.title: Refined grotesk
items.description: Neue-Montreal-like: a more considered, slightly humanist grotesk with subtle warmth over a purely mechanical sans.

items.title: Expressive display
items.description: Cabinet/Clash-like: a characterful display face with real personality, used for headlines to carry the brand voice.

items.title: Compressed statement
items.description: Monument-like: a tall, narrow, high-impact face for oversized headline moments.

items.title: Editorial serif + sans pairing
items.description: A serif for headlines or pull quotes paired with a sans for body and UI - a magazine register.

items.title: Swiss rational sans with hard hierarchy
items.description: A grid-disciplined sans with sharply stepped size/weight jumps and little ornament.

items.title: Cinematic centered minimalist
items.description: Centered headline over a strong single visual, generous negative space, minimal chrome.

items.title: Asymmetric split
items.description: Unequal left/right (or top/bottom) division between copy and visual - never a 50/50 default split.

items.title: Floating polaroid scatter
items.description: Multiple framed image tiles scattered/overlapping around the headline, giving a tactile, collected feel.

items.title: Inline typography behemoth
items.description: Oversized type IS the hero visual - little or no separate imagery, type carries the whole composition.

items.title: Editorial offset
items.description: Magazine-style offset grid where headline, subhead, and visual sit in deliberately uneven columns.

items.title: Massive image-first, restrained text
items.description: One huge image dominates; text is a small, confident accent rather than competing for space.

items.title: Giant statement
items.description: The headline fills most of the first screen at display scale; the visual supports it. Pair with type-led hero architectures and a short, punchy line.

items.title: Mid editorial
items.description: Headline at a confident but readable size sharing the first screen with a real visual and a short lead; the default for most product and content pages.

items.title: Mini minimalist
items.description: Small, quiet headline with wide empty ground or one dominant image; restraint is the statement. Pair with image-first or minimalist briefs.

items.title: Modular bento rhythm
items.description: Repeating grid of variable-size tiles/cards, bento-box style, across the page.

items.title: Alternating editorial blocks
items.description: Sections alternate text-left/image-right and the reverse, magazine-spread style.

items.title: Poster-stacked storytelling
items.description: Each section reads as its own full-bleed poster moment, stacked vertically as a sequence.

items.title: Gallery-led cadence
items.description: Image-forward sections paced like a gallery walk, with copy as captions rather than the lead.

items.title: Swiss grid discipline
items.description: A visible, consistent column grid governs every section - alignment is the whole personality.

items.title: Asymmetric premium flow
items.description: Sections vary width, alignment, and rhythm deliberately rather than repeating one template.

items.title: Diagonal staggered masonry
items.description: A tile grid staggered off the horizontal for tension instead of a flat masonry wall.

items.title: 3D cascading card deck
items.description: Cards fan out with depth/perspective like a dealt deck rather than a flat stack.

items.title: Hover-accordion slices
items.description: Vertical slices that expand on hover to reveal content, collapsing the rest.

items.title: Gapless bento
items.description: A bento grid with zero gutters, relying on internal padding and dividers for structure.

items.title: Brand marquee
items.description: A scrolling/looping strip of logos, words, or proof points as a horizontal band.

items.title: Turning polaroid arc
items.description: Framed images arranged along a gentle arc, each slightly rotated, like a fanned photo set.

items.title: Vertical rhythm lines
items.description: Thin vertical rules running through sections to mark rhythm/measurement, editorial-technical feel.

items.title: Off-grid editorial
items.description: A deliberate break from the grid for one component to create a focal moment.

items.title: Product UI panel stack
items.description: Layered mock product-UI panels stacked with depth, used when the brief is a product with a UI.

items.title: Split testimonial wall
items.description: Testimonials arranged in an uneven multi-column wall rather than a single centered carousel.

items.title: Oversized metrics strip
items.description: A band of large numerals/stats as a standalone proof section.

items.title: Layered image crop frames
items.description: Overlapping cropped image frames at different depths/scales within one composition.

items.title: Artifact / collectible
items.description: The product/brand is framed as a precious object to be examined and collected.

items.title: Journey / waypoints
items.description: The page reads as stops along a path, each section a waypoint in a larger route.

items.title: Tool / precision instrument
items.description: Technical, instrument-panel framing - the product as a precise tool, not a lifestyle object.

items.title: Living system / garden
items.description: Organic, growth-oriented framing - the product/brand as something cultivated over time.

items.title: Stage / spotlight
items.description: Theatrical framing - each section is a spotlighted moment on a dark or neutral stage.

items.title: Archive / dossier
items.description: Documentary, case-file framing - content presented as evidence in a dossier.

items.title: Asymmetric bleed
items.description: One element deliberately bleeds off the grid/edge where nothing else does, creating a single surprise.

items.title: Oversized numeral or punctuation as structure
items.description: A single giant numeral or punctuation mark used as a structural/layout device, not just decoration.

items.title: One material switch
items.description: Exactly one section swaps the page's material language (texture, finish) to mark a turn in the story.

items.title: Narrow vertical side-rail note
items.description: A thin marginal column carrying an annotation, aside, or footnote-style detail.

items.title: Macro crop carrying the brand color
items.description: An extreme close-up crop used once, saturated in the brand's accent color, as a texture break.
